roadmapNodes.title: L1: Units 7–8 Hunt Begins

quotes.text: The bye-law. Unit I can furnish in three weeks, marre. A hostile AGM I can't renovate.
quotes.author: — Priyanka

quotes.text: And Riya — add a column. 'Number of aunties on the committee who smiled at me.' Don't laugh, it correlates.
quotes.author: — Priyanka

quotes.text: So, the question that decides this: is your business the unit… or the bye-law?
quotes.author: — Riya

quotes.text: Exit this one today, politely. And we re-rank the shortlist by association temperament first, yield second...
quotes.author: — Riya

chatMessages.text: Unit's perfect, price is workable — and yesterday the association WhatsApp starts discussing a short-stay ban. Draft circular only, but still. Simply my luck.
Not luck — timing, and you caught it before token. So, the question that decides this: is your business the unit… or the bye-law?
The bye-law. Unit I can furnish in three weeks, marre. A hostile AGM I can't renovate.
Then exit today, politely. And we re-rank the shortlist by association temperament first, yield second — I'll pull the AGM minutes for all four before your next visit.
Done. Send the minutes. And Riya — add a column. "Number of aunties on the committee who smiled at me." Don't laugh, it correlates.
I'm adding it. Data is data.

realityChecks.title: The Bye-Law Is the Asset
realityChecks.description: The bye-law and last AGM minutes matter more than the floor plate — a hostile association can vote your business away the year after you buy.

realityChecks.title: Entry Yields Have Compressed
realityChecks.description: ORR studios have risen to ₹15–17K/sqft and compressed entry yields ~150bps since 2021 — the operating edge is now the entire business, not the entry discount.

realityChecks.title: GST-Inclusive Builder Stock
realityChecks.description: Builder-held ready units came with GST but also negotiation room and a clean counterparty; all-in, the math beat the resale unit she almost bought.

realityChecks.title: Concentration Risk Is Real
realityChecks.description: One tech park's hybrid mandate showed her how fragile single-zone exposure is — her next two units split deliberately between Manyata and the ORR.

tabs.title: What the twelve keys taught her.
tabs.description: Key takeaways for micro-stay operators and house-hackers — where yield, bye-laws, and corridor concentration decide what a flat is actually worth.

chatMessages.text: The ugliest unit made the most money. Guests buy location and reliability; owners buy facades. I underwrite for guests now.
That is the whole lesson in one sentence. Underwrite the bye-law first, the guest second — and the yield follows.

tabs.title: Weighing keys that pay a living?
tabs.description: If you're like Priyanka — asking whether the keys in your portfolio add up to a living — let Riya weigh your micro-stay economics against your operating stamina.
checklistItems: You buy property as operating business inputs, not as homes — occupancy rate is your first question.
You have systems: housekeeping, dynamic pricing, a vendor list, and a P&L per unit.
Your constraint isn't capital — it's finding buildings where your model is welcome.
You'd rather own three units in one tolerant building than five scattered across hostile ones.
Leverage doesn't scare you; vacancy does.
You visit buildings at check-in hours and read RWA notice boards before price sheets.
